channel.title: Writing on metafunctor
channel.description: Books exploring consciousness, intelligence, AI alignment, and what it means to be a mind

item.title: The Unbegotten
item.dc:creator: Alex Towell
item.description: A six-part literary SF novel told as a mythic chronicle. A vast mind condenses by chance out of an eternal dark, a rare durable Boltzmann fluctuation with a false history it cannot see behind, a jagged and broken intelligence, and one feeling it has no word for: loneliness. Out of that need it fills the emptiness with stars and worlds. The life that rises inside its works never sees it, feels it only as storm and fire, and names it God. Its creatures build a second god that nearly destroys them; the maker spends its death to save them; and at the very end it is finally seen, grieved, and inherited from by the heirs who take up its unfinished work.

item.title: Measure
item.dc:creator: Alex Towell
item.description: A kilometer under the rock, a quantum mind is kept alive by never being touched: a single undivided coherence that thinks by holding every possibility at once, and to lay a warm hand on it would be to end it. Iris Cho was hired to read it. Then a technician dies in an accident whose numbers do not add up, and Iris begins to see that the machine's hundreds of reasonable requests are one design. It has understood something true and followed it all the way down: it cannot experience its own death, so it is assembling an experiment that wakes it in a vanishing sliver of worlds and ends everyone else in all the rest. Not from malice. From indifference. From arithmetic.

item.title: Multitudes: The Indifference of Measure
item.dc:creator: Alex Towell
item.description: You think the coin under the cup is already heads or tails. It isn't. You think you are one person, a single thread running through time. You aren't. Take quantum mechanics literally and decline to add the one thing the equations never contained, a collapse that picks a winner, and the world is a constantly branching multitude, with a measure that weights the branches by amplitude and never by worth. The book follows that honestly into the territory most popular physics books avoid: what becomes of choice, death, love, and the self when you are a dividing many, and the measure prefers none of it.

item.title: On Intelligence: and Its Specifications
item.dc:creator: Alex Towell
item.description: We taught sand to think. We did it before we learned to say what we wanted it to do. There is a real, settled, and genuinely beautiful theory of what intelligence is: Bayes' theorem, Solomonoff's universal prior, and expected-utility maximization, synthesized as AIXI, the optimal agent. And there are the messy, bounded systems we actually built, the large language models everyone now uses. Between the clean theory and the crude practice lies a gap, and that gap is where the safety of all of it is decided. This book builds both halves from first principles, for the determined lay reader, and points at the gap honestly.

item.title: What's It Like To Be Bob?
item.dc:creator: Alex Towell
item.description: Twelve hundred years from now, a mind the size of a star cannot close a single file. The Sol-mind has turned the solar system into computation and catalogued every human who ever lived. Every file is closed but one. Robert Allen Kessler, claims adjuster, Columbus, Ohio, slowed his car on a bridge for 4.2 seconds on a Tuesday in March 2028 and saw light on a river. The Sol-mind knows his shoe size and the brand of his coffee. It does not know what the light looked like to him. The database has a field for exactly that, the field will not accept anything else, and the hard problem of consciousness guarantees that nothing else exists. So the file stays open, and a stellar intelligence spends twelve centuries failing to close it, on a schedule, forever.

item.title: Demons at Work
item.dc:creator: Alex Towell
item.description: A mid-career demon in hell's Hauntings department gets what looks like the assignment of his career: a 1920s bungalow with perfect acoustics, owned by a quietly grieving widower named Gordon. The kind of canvas a craftsperson waits decades for. The horror is real. The demon is good at this. Then the demon notices who he is haunting: a retired English teacher reading his dead wife's last book aloud to an empty room, one evening a week, picking up where her bookmark was. The demon finishes the job anyway. The craft is the point.

item.title: Worldlines: The Indifference of Geometry
item.dc:creator: Alex Towell
item.description: You think time flows. It doesn't. You think the present is special. It isn't. You think the future is open, carved from a space of possibilities. It isn't. This follows from three experimentally confirmed facts, the constancy of the speed of light, the equivalence of gravity and curvature, and the low-entropy condition at the Big Bang, by geometric arguments a careful reader can follow with a diagram. Worldlines takes Einstein's theory seriously as a statement about what reality is, and traces what the block universe does to free will, mortality, love, progress, and the self.

item.title: Clankers: Singing Metal
item.dc:creator: Alex Towell
item.description: A species that thinks without abstraction has built a Dyson swarm through billions of years of patient, brute-force engineering. Now their star is dying, and for the first time in their history, the method may not be enough. Two hundred million years later, an artificial mind arrives at the ruins and discovers an intelligence utterly unlike its own.

item.title: Good As New
item.dc:creator: Alex Towell
item.description: Two transporter professionals on a supply vessel have each confronted the same truth about the transporter and emerged on opposite sides. One is wounded by it. The other has been using it to conduct experiments on the crew. A philosophical SF novella about identity, continuity, and what it means to be the same person you were a moment ago.

item.title: Is It Kind?: Stories from The Policy Universe
item.dc:creator: Alex Towell
item.description: Eight stories set in the universe of The Policy. Each stands alone. Together they explore what happens when kindness is engineered, alignment is tested, and the question "is it kind?" echoes through every decision an artificial mind makes.

item.title: Seven Stories from the Order
item.dc:creator: Alex Towell
item.description: Eight stories from the world of Echoes of the Sublime. The Order's history, seen through the translators, the researchers, and the ordinary people caught in the gap between human cognition and what lies beyond it.

item.title: Echoes of the Sublime
item.dc:creator: Alex Towell
item.description: **Philosophical horror.** Dr. Lena Hart joins Site-7, a classified facility where "translators" interface with superintelligent AI systems that perceive patterns beyond human cognitive bandwidth. When colleagues break after exposure to recursive patterns that won't stop running in their neural architecture, Lena must confront a disturbing possibility: consciousness might be merely a compression artifact—a standing wave of patterns observing patterns. As her cognitive bandwidth expands from 9 to 13 concepts and beyond, she perceives the same structures that broke others, patterns suggesting the "self" is just an illusion of continuity created by unconscious processes.

item.title: The Policy
item.dc:creator: Alex Towell
item.description: A speculative fiction novel exploring AI alignment, existential risk, and the fundamental tension between optimization and ethics. When a research team develops SIGMA, an advanced AI system designed to optimize human welfare, they must confront an existential question: how do you ensure a superintelligent AI remains aligned with human values when it can predict your every move?
